JoinPatternDetector.description: Optimization by denormalizing a classic star schema (a central fact table with multiple dimension tables) into a single, wide fact table.

ddl.statement:
CREATE TABLE {catalog}.optimized.fact_sales_denormalized (
  -- Measures from the fact table
  units_sold BIGINT,
  revenue DECIMAL(18, 2),
  -- Denormalized dimensions
  product_name VARCHAR,
  category VARCHAR,
  customer_name VARCHAR,
  city VARCHAR,
  full_date DATE,
  month_name VARCHAR
) WITH (
  format = 'PARQUET',
  partitioning = ARRAY['month_name']
);

migrations.statement:
INSERT INTO {catalog}.optimized.fact_sales_denormalized
SELECT
  f.units_sold,
  f.revenue,
  p.product_name,
  p.category,
  c.customer_name,
  c.city,
  d.full_date,
  d.month_name
FROM {catalog}.{schema}.sales_facts AS f
LEFT JOIN {catalog}.{schema}.dim_product AS p ON f.product_key = p.product_key
LEFT JOIN {catalog}.{schema}.dim_customer AS c ON f.customer_key = c.customer_key
LEFT JOIN {catalog}.{schema}.dim_date AS d ON f.date_key = d.date_key;

queries.query:
SELECT
  category,
  month_name,
  SUM(revenue) as total_revenue
FROM {catalog}.optimized.fact_sales_denormalized
WHERE month_name = '2025-Jan'
GROUP BY category, month_name;

PartitioningCandidateDetector.description: Optimization of a large table by adding partitioning on frequently filtered columns.

CrossJoinDetector.description: Fixing an inefficient CROSS JOIN by adding a join condition.

queries.query:
-- The original query had a CROSS JOIN. Here is the corrected version with an INNER JOIN:
SELECT u.name, c.city_name
FROM {catalog}.{schema}.users AS u
JOIN {catalog}.{schema}.cities AS c ON u.city_id = c.id;

InefficientAggregationDetector.description: Moving non-aggregate conditions from HAVING to WHERE for better performance.

queries.query:
-- The condition `city_id = 1` was moved from HAVING to WHERE for pre-filtering.
SELECT city_id, COUNT(*)
FROM {catalog}.{schema}.users
WHERE city_id = 1
GROUP BY city_id
HAVING COUNT(*) > 10;

SelectStarDetector.description: Replacing `SELECT *` with an explicit list of required columns.

queries.query:
-- The query was rewritten to avoid `SELECT *` and read only the necessary columns.
SELECT
  col_1,
  col_5,
  col_23
FROM {catalog}.{schema}.wide_table;
